name: IN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+15
Incumbent Jim Baird running for reelection with a large financial edge
Democrat Drew Cox has raised only about $20,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price Baird's win probability at roughly 94%
model.rationale: This is a solidly Republican seat where Baird holds the incumbency advantage and has out-raised Cox by more than 17-to-1, while Cox's minimal war chest and lack of outside backing give him little means to close the gap. Markets and the district's fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic outside spending or a major scandal involving Baird would be the main ways this race could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 4th District is a heavily Republican seat, and incumbent Jim Baird is seeking another term. He has the advantages that typically come with incumbency in favorable terrain: name recognition, a district lean of roughly fifteen points toward his party, and a fundraising operation that dwarfs his opponent's. Drew Cox has raised about $20,000 and reports minimal cash on hand, with no outside groups supporting his campaign.

Baird, by contrast, has raised over $350,000 and benefits from more than $500,000 in outside spending on his behalf, though outside groups have also spent against him. Prediction markets give Cox only a small chance of an upset. With no public polling available, the picture rests on the district's fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing, all of which point to a Republican hold.
